newsitem.title: UK: British publisher offers Clinton coat of arms.
newsitem.headline: British publisher offers Clinton coat of arms.

text.p: An aristocratic British publisher on Monday unveiled the coat of arms it proposes for President Bill Clinton, saying he was the only head of a major country not to have some such "devise of heraldry".
Burke's Peerage said it hoped to present the coat of arms to Clinton, either on vellum (calf skin) or parchment, "at a future date".
Its design, which it is offering to amend at Clinton's behest, incorporates a range of symbols of the president's family and of the United States.
His wife Hillary is represented by the red lion of St Hillary of Poitiers, France, and his daughter Chelsea by the anchor mark of the British china of that name.
A bald eagle symbolising the United States holds in its talons a cross and a mullet, emblems of the ancient English and Irish families of Clinton.
Two white rabbits represent, say Burke's Peerage, the fecundity of the American nation.

The shield at the centre of the coat of arms has two "supporters" -- an Indian chief in full feather headdress carrying a peace pipe, and an unchained black woman, representing freedom from slavery and from male domination.
"There are many symbols in Mr Clinton's coat of arms which will inspire America and the world in the 21st century," said the firm's publishing director, Harold Brooks-Baker.
